subject: Task 17.4 / Phase 17 (Goal F3, ADR-025 clause 6): the shipped read-only diagnostics status surface - the elevation-gated GET ArrTags/Status endpoint (ArrTagsStatusController), the bounded DiagnosticsSnapshot / MatchingFailureCounts / RenderFailureCounts / DiagnosticsMetrics / DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider model, the counter instrumentation sites (RadarrMetadataReader, SonarrMetadataReader, ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader, MetadataReconciliationProcessor, ArtworkGenerationCoordinator, ArrConnectionHealthMapping), and the read-only settings-page diagnostics panel in Configuration/config.html. Audited against ADR-025 clauses 1-6, docs/planning/v1.2.md Goal F3 and section 9, docs/architecture/11, docs/architecture/12, and the 17.4 documentation surfaces (README, ADR-025 implementation note, limitations archive F3).

findings.description: The canonical documentation states without qualification that a malformed response/body leaves the diagnostics panel with no data, but the shipped panel only fail-closes on unparseable or non-object JSON. The guard at config.html:598 accepts any non-null non-array object, and the readers at config.html:568-593 return the code-owned 0 / 'Unknown' fallbacks for missing or non-numeric fields; a 200 response that is a well-formed JSON object of the wrong or partial shape (for example '{}' or '{"QueueDepth":5}') therefore renders the full fixed 28-row table with 0/'Unknown' values and makes the panel visible (config.html:641). The README states 'a malformed response leaves the panel showing no data' (README.md:148); architecture 11 and 12 say the panel 'renders no data ... when the route is unauthorized, unavailable, or malformed (fail-closed)' (docs/architecture/11-failure-consistency-and-security-policy.md:62-64, docs/architecture/12-performance-and-operational-limits.md:192-194); the F3 archive entry says 'a malformed body leave[s] it cleared' (docs/limitations/archive.md:202-204); and the ADR-025 implementation note says the panel 'clears on a rejected/unavailable request or a malformed body' (docs/decisions/ADR-025.md:109-110). ADJUDICATION: this is a documentation-precision and optional-hardening gap, not an exploitable defect. There is no secret exposure, no error surface, and no free-form response text: the render domain is the fixed page table, the only values written are a finite JSON number or a declared ArrConnectionHealth name, and the response object is never iterated or stringified. Reachability in production is nil because the same-origin endpoint always serializes the fixed DiagnosticsSnapshot; a wrong-shape object could only come from a contract regression or a same-origin route shadow, and the shipped fallback behavior is deliberate per the task 17.3 interpretation ('tolerating a missing field with a safe fallback (0/Unknown) rather than failing'). The gap is that the unconditional 'malformed' wording does not distinguish 'unparseable / non-object' (fail-closed) from 'well-formed wrong-shape object' (fallback table), and the fail-closed test only asserts the non-object cases (tests/ArrTags.Tests/DiagnosticsStatusPanelTests.cs:151-186).

findings.recommended_action: Non-blocking. Either (a) tighten the wording in README.md:148, docs/architecture/11:62-64, docs/architecture/12:192-194, docs/limitations/archive.md:202-204, and the ADR-025 implementation note to 'an unparseable or non-object response' and state the documented 0/'Unknown' fallback for a missing field, or (b) add an explicit fixed-shape guard in diagnosticsRenderPanel (require the expected top-level counter objects before showing the panel) so any wrong-shape body leaves the panel cleared, and add a structural test for the wrong-shape-object case either way. No secret, state, or authorization consequence either way.

findings.description: The panel's inline JavaScript is never executed by the test suite or the documented pinned-host live matrix: the repository deliberately has no JavaScript runtime and the pinned matrix runs --nowebclient, so the fetch, the web client's rejection path, the DOM construction, and the fail-closed no-data rendering are pinned structurally only (against the endpoint model and the pinned bundled web-client source). The residual is disclosed honestly in the ADR-025 implementation note (docs/decisions/ADR-025.md:119-128), the F3 archive verification bounds (docs/limitations/archive.md:219-227), the task 17.4 changelog entry (docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md:1068-1077), and the 17.3/17.4 reports, and the plan assigns pinned-host live verification to Phase 21 task 21.4. However, because that live matrix runs --nowebclient, it will not execute the panel JavaScript either, so this is a standing v1.2 verification limitation rather than a phase-verification boundary. It is not in the limitation register, so the register and docs/status.md do not carry it. The established precedent is V12-G8-1, which registered the analogous web-client modal reminder ('verified structurally, not executed') as an accepted LOW in docs/limitations/accepted.md, docs/limitations/00-index.md, and docs/plan/state.json limitations.accepted. ADJUDICATION: the residual is genuinely acceptable (the panel's security-relevant behavior is enforced by shipped code rather than by convention: fixed table, textContent-only DOM writes, bounded numeric/enum readers, clear-on-rejection), but it should not be accepted silently.

findings.description: Assessment of whether the in-process MVC test honestly represents host enforcement: yes, for the attribute-to-policy evaluation, with the host-side middleware and policy definition not executed here. The status controller is class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)] with no [AllowAnonymous] at class or action level and exactly one [HttpGet] action (src/ArrTags/Diagnostics/ArrTagsStatusController.cs:27-59); the pipeline harness registers a policy with the pinned host shape (authenticated principal plus the Administrator role claim), disables endpoint routing so MVC's AuthorizeFilter enforces the same [Authorize] metadata the host's AuthorizationMiddleware enforces, and reproduces 401 (anonymous, empty body), 403 (authenticated non-administrator, empty body), and 200 (administrator, body equal to the live snapshot) (tests/ArrTags.Tests/DiagnosticsStatusEndpointTests.cs:434-530, 206-254). I independently verified from the pinned Jellyfin revision 6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc that Jellyfin.Server/Extensions/ApiServiceCollectionExtensions.cs AddJellyfinApiAuthorization defines Policies.RequiresElevation as the custom-authentication scheme plus RequireClaim(ClaimTypes.Role, UserRoles.Administrator), and that AddJellyfinApi adds plugin assemblies as MVC application parts and activates controllers through DI (AddControllersAsServices), so the host's policy definition matches the harness policy shape. The host-guarded policy-name fact (tests/ArrTags.Tests/DiagnosticsStatusEndpointTests.cs:256-274) skips because ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset, so live host-side authorization is not confirmed in this environment; the residual is disclosed in the ADR-025 implementation note, the F3 archive bounds, the changelog, and the 17.2/17.4 reports, and the v1.2 plan assigns the live pinned-host verification to Phase 21 task 21.4. No alternate unauthenticated path exists: the only other plugin controller is the by-design anonymous webhook route, which authenticates the shared secret before any body read (src/ArrTags/Webhooks/ArrTagsWebhookController.cs:32-35, 110-141).

findings.description: The 17.2 worker report recorded the host MVC JSON options as a precondition ('the host configures MVC JSON options as the pinned revision does'). I resolved it from the pinned host source and by independent serialization rather than leaving it as an assumption. At revision 6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc, Jellyfin.Server/Extensions/ApiServiceCollectionExtensions.cs AddJellyfinApi copies JsonDefaults.PascalCaseOptions converters and PropertyNamingPolicy into the MVC JSON options and registers PascalCaseJsonProfileFormatter (supporting application/json) at output-formatter index 0, ahead of the camelCase profile formatter; src/Jellyfin.Extensions/Json/JsonDefaults.cs sets PascalCaseOptions.PropertyNamingPolicy to null (PascalCase) and includes JsonStringEnumConverter plus the Jellyfin enum converter factories. My independent probe (/tmp/17.4-sec/jsonprobe, referencing the built plugin project and Jellyfin.Controller 12.0.0) serialized the live DiagnosticsSnapshot with JsonDefaults.Options and produced exactly the fixed 28 leaf paths: 26 JSON numbers and two string leaves (SonarrHealth/RadarrHealth as 'Healthy'/'Unavailable'), with PascalCase names. The panel's table and health whitelist match that shape exactly. A client that explicitly requests application/json; profile="CamelCase" would receive camelCase (the panel does not request that profile and, if it ever did, would fall back to the SR-17.4-01 0/'Unknown' rendering); a text/xml request would be handled by the host's XmlOutputFormatter, which writes Object.ToString() (the type name, no data). Neither changes the bounded, secret-free field set.

findings.description: The task-15.4 security review's LOW finding SR-15.4-01 remains open by explicit decision: control-scalar removal in the bounded log subject is Unicode Cc only, so Cf format characters (for example U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE, U+200B) and the Zl/Zp separators (U+2028/U+2029) pass through a media file name into the log line, which is a log-integrity/readability weakness with no secret exposure and no effect on the bounded volume. The behavior is recorded as the intended literal ADR-026 clause 2 reading in the ADR-026 implementation note; SR-15.4-02's recommended README qualification was applied (README.md:97 now scopes the directory/full-path exclusion to a host-native media path). Phase 17 changes no logging call site (the phase diff adds no _log.Write/LogLevel line; the only IArrTagsLog mentions are pre-existing constructor signatures), and the diagnostics counters are numeric and are never logged, so this carried finding is unchanged by, and unrelated to, the diagnostics surface.

Counter inputs are bounded enums/indices only: RecordRenderFailure/RecordProviderHealth reject out-of-range or undefined values, RecordMatchingFailure ignores non-failure statuses, and no item-keyed counter or per-item collection exists, so a high-cardinality input cannot amplify or grow the counter set

The counters are 64-bit and monotonic; overflow would require ~9.2e18 increments per counter and is not reachable by bounded work or by endpoint reads (reads do not increment)

summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; no open BLOCKER or HIGH, so the Phase 17 gate condition (security review with no open BLOCKER/HIGH) is met. The shipped read-only diagnostics surface is authorized, read-only, bounded, and secret-free as the ADR-025 contract requires. Authorization: one class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)] GET route with no [AllowAnonymous] and no write verb; the in-process MVC pipeline reproduces 401/403/200 with empty rejection bodies, the pinned host's RequiresElevation policy definition and plugin application-part registration were verified from the pinned source, and the only other plugin controller is the by-design secret-authenticated webhook route. The host-guarded policy-name fact is skipped here (ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR unset) and the host AuthorizationMiddleware path is not executed; that residual is disclosed in the ADR-025 note, the F3 archive bounds, and the changelog, and is assigned to the Phase 21.4 live matrix. Secret-freedom and bounded shape: an independent serialization of the live snapshot with JsonDefaults.Options produced exactly the fixed 28 leaf paths (26 numbers plus the two declared ArrConnectionHealth string names), the model graph contains no string/path/identifier/collection carrier, and no per-item or item-keyed counter exists, so attacker-influenced cardinality cannot amplify the counters. The endpoint performs O(1) work with no provider/render/library I/O, no input, no persistence, and no state mutation. The panel renders only the fixed table and bounded values via textContent, contains no secret literal and no input/save wiring, starts hidden/empty, and clears on rejection; it never renders a free-form response string. Documentation honesty is good: the three verification bounds (inline JS unexecuted, host-guarded fact skipped, process-lifetime counters) are stated in the archive entry, ADR-025 note, and changelog, and the counter set is recorded as the clause 3 contract. Two non-blocking LOW findings remain open: SR-17.4-01 (the docs' unconditional 'malformed response leaves no data' wording is not guaranteed for a well-formed wrong-shape JSON object, which renders the documented 0/'Unknown' fallback table; no secret, error surface, or injection is involved) and SR-17.4-02 (the panel's structural-only verification is disclosed but not registered; recommend accepted limitation V12-F3-1 in the V12-G8-1 pattern with the accepted.md/00-index.md/state.json.accepted/status.md surfaces named). Two informational notes record the authorization evidence assessment and the resolved host-JSON precondition; the carried task-15.4 log-path LOW (SR-15.4-01) is unchanged and outside this surface. No production code, test, or documentation was modified by this review; the only artifact written is this report.
